systems: EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) — high-risk obligations, in force 2 Aug 2026
Prohibited AI practices (Art. 5) — social scoring, emotion recognition, real-time biometric ID
SCHUFA credit scoring — automated individual decision-making (Art. 22 GDPR / CJEU C-634/21), AI Act high-risk
Predictive policing software (Hesse/Hamburg) — struck down by German Constitutional Court
highlights: EU AI Act high-risk rules + AI Office enforcement live from 2 August 2026 (official page updated 3 Aug 2026).
Nine prohibited practices (Art. 5) including social scoring and emotion recognition have been banned since 2 Feb 2025.
CJEU C-634/21: SCHUFA credit-score creation is automated decision-making under Art. 22 GDPR; SCHUFA cut criteria from ~250 to 12 on 17 Mar 2026; creditworthiness AI is high-risk from Aug 2026.
German Constitutional Court (16 Feb 2023) declared Hesse/Hamburg predictive-policing software unconstitutional.
actions_taken: researched EU AI Act, Art. 5 prohibitions, SCHUFA/CJEU, predictive policing via web (official EU + primary sources)
opened PR against main (human review only — not merged)
